items.title: Tesla Deploys 13.5 GWh of Storage in Q2 2026
items.summary: Tesla announced it deployed 13.5 GWh of energy storage products globally in Q2 2026, a sharp jump from the 8.8 GWh delivered in Q1 and up significantly year-over-year. The company set its Q2 earnings webcast for July 22, where investors are expected to press for details on its VPP partnership with Sunrun and Renew Home.

items.title: Alpiq to Acquire 90% Stake in Harmony Energy
items.summary: Swiss power company Alpiq has agreed to acquire a 90% stake in UK-based battery storage developer-operator Harmony Energy, consolidating its position in the European BESS market.

items.title: Frontier Power USA Converts 920 MWh Texas BESS Portfolio
items.summary: Frontier Power USA exercised its selection right to convert four battery storage projects from Stella Energy Solutions—the Blanquilla, Aransas Pass, Nash and Wallis projects—representing roughly 230 MW/920 MWh of capacity. The projects are expected to use Eos Energy's Z3 long-duration batteries, though closing depends on Eos completing its rights offering.

items.title: BYD and Greenvolt to Build 2.4 GWh Poland Storage Site
items.summary: BYD Energy Storage and Greenvolt Power will co-develop a 600 MW/2.4 GWh energy storage facility in Siedlce, Poland, with construction planned to begin in the third quarter of 2026 and operations targeted by the end of 2027.

items.title: Chinese Integrators Hold 76% of Global BESS Market
items.summary: New industry data shows Chinese system integrators cemented their dominance of the global battery energy storage market, capturing 76% of global market share in 2025, underscoring the country's continued lead in equipment supply even as installation growth slows domestically.

items.title: CATL Secures 60 GWh Sodium-Ion Supply Deal
items.summary: CATL has confirmed sodium-ion cells will reach mass production in 2026 and has secured a 60 GWh sodium-ion supply contract, reportedly the largest single order for sodium cells globally. The company projects sodium-ion could eventually displace 30-40% of the battery market while matching LFP energy density at potentially lower cost.

items.title: NUS Researchers Advance Safer Solid-State Sodium Battery
items.summary: Researchers at the National University of Singapore developed a composite polymer electrolyte that improves sodium-ion transport and compatibility with sodium metal in all-solid-state cells, addressing safety limitations that have held back the technology. The team is now working to optimize the cells for stable operation near ambient temperatures around 45°C.

items.title: Peak Energy, ESS Tech, Unigrid Push Sodium-Ion Forward
items.summary: Three companies—Peak Energy, ESS Tech Inc, and Unigrid—made fresh announcements this week advancing sodium-ion energy storage technology across the US and Europe, reflecting accelerating momentum behind the lithium alternative for grid-scale applications.

items.title: Elestor Deploys Hydrogen-Iron Flow Battery in Netherlands
items.summary: Dutch long-duration storage developer Elestor partnered with Windpark Zeewolde to deploy a 20MW/200-800MWh hydrogen-iron flow battery system at what is described as Europe's largest onshore wind farm, marking a significant demonstration of flow battery technology at scale.

items.title: L-H Battery Starts Li-ion Cell Production in Ohio
items.summary: L-H Battery Company began lithium-ion cell production this month at its Jeffersonville, Ohio plant, targeting both automotive and stationary power storage applications as domestic US cell manufacturing capacity continues to expand.

items.title: FERC Orders Six Grid Operators to Reform Large-Load Tariffs
items.summary: FERC issued show cause orders under Section 206 to all six regional grid operators, directing them to justify or reform tariffs governing how data centers and other large energy users connect to the grid. Each operator has 60 days to justify current rules or propose changes covering interconnection speed, cost-shifting prevention, and co-location agreements.

items.title: New Jersey Enacts Data Center Tariff and Grid Reform Bills
items.summary: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill signed three bills into law aimed at cutting transmission owners' return on equity, establishing dedicated data center tariffs, and requiring state approval for supplemental transmission projects. The data center tariff law requires utilities to incentivize large users to bring their own clean generation or energy storage and to offset capacity obligations through behind-the-meter storage and demand response.

items.title: Vietnam Adopts Two-Part Tariff for Battery Storage
items.summary: With the implementation of Circular No. 62/2025/TT-BCT in January 2026, Vietnam became the first major ASEAN economy to introduce a formal two-part tariff structure for battery energy storage systems, paying batteries for both capacity availability and energy delivery rather than energy alone.

items.title: Australia Adds First Nations Pilot to Storage Tenders
items.summary: The Australian federal government has introduced a dedicated First Nations Set Aside pilot program into both Capacity Investment Scheme Tenders 9 and 10, aiming to broaden participation in the country's large-scale storage and renewables procurement rounds.

items.title: FERC Holds Technical Conference on Grid-Enhancing Tech
items.summary: FERC held a supplemental technical conference on July 7-8, 2026 to discuss grid-enhancing technologies, load forecasting, and opportunities to boost market and planning efficiency through improved software, part of its broader push to modernize grid operations amid rising demand.
